::: {.teacher-key}
The buzzer and horn currents are stated modelling assumptions. Confirm the
actual device voltage, current, polarity, acoustic risk, and supply/fuse ratings
before a demonstration. The LED investigation is the required student build.
:::

## 1. Discharge-loop KVL

Using the indicated voltage polarities:

$$
+V_C-V_{R1}-V_{LED}=0
$$

or $V_C=V_{R1}+V_{LED}$. As $V_C$ falls, LED current falls and the simple fixed
forward-voltage model becomes less accurate.

## 2. Node-A KCL

While S1 is closed:

$$
I_{RC}=I_C+I_{LED}
$$

For the optional buzzer branch, replace $I_{LED}$ with the appropriate verified
load current. Current directions must be defined consistently.

## 3. Stored energy

$1000\ \mu\mathrm{F}=0.001000$ F.

$$
E_C=\frac{1}{2}CV^2=\frac{1}{2}(0.001000)(5.0)^2=0.0125\ \mathrm{J}
$$

## 4. Buzzer support estimate

$$
\Delta t\approx\frac{C\Delta V}{I}
=\frac{(0.001000)(5.0-3.0)}{0.012}=0.167\ \mathrm{s}
$$

The real duration may differ because buzzer current is not constant, the buzzer
has a minimum operating voltage, the capacitor has tolerance and internal
resistance, and circuit resistance causes additional voltage loss.

## 5. Measured KVL check

Answers depend on student measurements. Accept a clearly labelled check of
$V_C-(V_{R1}+V_{LED})$ with meter resolution and changing capacitor voltage
considered. Measurements taken at widely separated times should not be treated
as simultaneous.

## 6. Automotive capacitance estimate

$$
C\approx\frac{I\Delta t}{\Delta V}
=\frac{(5.0)(0.250)}{4.0}=0.3125\ \mathrm{F}
$$

$$
0.3125\ \mathrm{F}=312{,}500\ \mu\mathrm{F}
$$

This is an idealized lower-order estimate, not a recommended capacitor value.

## 7. Energy and comparison

$$
E=\frac{1}{2}(0.3125)(12.0)^2=22.5\ \mathrm{J}
$$

Capacitance ratio:

$$
\frac{312{,}500\ \mu\mathrm{F}}{1000\ \mu\mathrm{F}}=312.5
$$

The estimate requires over 300 times the student capacitor's capacitance.
Actual performance also depends on equivalent series resistance, surge current,
horn behaviour, temperature, wiring, and the horn's minimum useful voltage.

## 8. Timing versus energy

The RC network produces a changing low-energy control voltage. A threshold or
switching driver converts that voltage into a definite command for the relay
coil. The relay provides electrical separation between its coil and contacts.
The fused 12 V source, load wiring, contacts, and return carry horn current. The
timing capacitor does not carry or supply the horn's load current.

## Calculation checks

| Quantity | Check |
|---|---:|
| 1000 µF energy at 5 V | 0.0125 J |
| ideal 12 mA buzzer estimate, 5 V to 3 V | 0.167 s |
| horn estimate | 0.3125 F = 312,500 µF |
| estimated energy at 12 V | 22.5 J |
| capacitance ratio | 312.5:1 |
